title: Multi-tenant KV cache allocation & savings matrix
summary: Working spreadsheet exploring how to allocate a shared KV/prefix cache across multiple tenants (customer accounts / endpoints) and estimate per-tenant and aggregate cost savings under different hit-rate, quota, and eviction-policy assumptions. Emphasis on realistic multi-tenant behavior: skew, burstiness, and cross-tenant cold starts.
assumptions: 1) Cache is a single shared LRU with optional per-tenant reserved slots. 2) Baseline per-token model cost = $0.0008 (hosted equivalent), host latency and throughput unaffected by small cache adjustments. 3) Workloads characterized by: tail-heavy (10% of tenants produce 80% of traffic), steady-state vs burst windows, median sequence length 64 tokens. 4) Hit -> 90% token-level cost removed; misses -> full model invoke. 5) Prefetch increases hit probability for sequences with stable prefixes but has a CPU/IO prefetch cost estimated as 0.02x per-token. 6) Quantized model variants have different per-token costs; this sheet assumes homogeneous model family for baseline scenarios.
methodology: We simulate a month of requests per tenant using three traffic shapes (steady, spiky, and periodic). For each allocation policy (shared-only, reserved per-tenant, proportional-reserve, dynamic-target), we compute: 1) per-tenant hit-rate, 2) model-invocations avoided, 3) gross token-cost reduction, 4) prefetch/management overhead, 5) net savings, 6) effective savings per $1 committed capacity. Eviction behavior modeled with per-tenant key counts and reuse intervals. Monte Carlo runs (n=1000) produce percentile bands used to populate the scenario matrix.
scenario_highlights: Shared-only LRU: best aggregate hit-rate for heavy-skew workloads, but small tenants can see 0-5% hit-rate causing poor product UX
Proportional-reserve (percent of cache reserved by historical p95 traffic): reduces small-tenant variance but reduces aggregate hit-rate by 6-12% depending on skew

Dynamic-target (auto reassign slots based on recent 1h usage + min-reserve): preserves heavy-tenant efficiency while guaranteeing soft floor for low-traffic tenants; 65-80% of peak savings of shared-only with far lower small-tenant tail risk
Prefetch windows of 3–7 tokens improve hit-rate by 4–10% on stable conversational workloads but cost ~0.5–1.3% net due to CPU prefetch overhead for low-reuse tenants
Burst isolation (per-tenant burst caps) prevents noisy neighbors from evicting hot entries, improving tail latency but reduces instantaneous aggregate token savings during bursts.
numeric_examples:
Example extract (single run median):
- Fleet: 100 tenants, top-10 tenants = 72% of tokens. Total monthly tokens: 1.2B.
- Baseline model cost (no cache): $960,000
- Shared-only LRU: aggregate hit-rate 28% -> gross model cost reduction $268,800; prefetch overhead $0 -> net $268,800 (28% savings)
- Proportional-reserve (10% reserved per tenant by historical share): aggregate hit-rate 22% -> gross saving $211,200; overhead $0 -> net $211,200 (22% savings); small tenants median hit-rate increases from 3% -> 9%
- Dynamic-target w/ min-reserve 1%: aggregate hit-rate 24.5% -> gross saving $235,200; prefetch overhead (prefetch enabled for top-20 tenants) $6,000 -> net $229,200 (~23.9% savings); median small-tenant hit-rate 7%
- Prefetch-only (no reserve): +6% absolute hit-rate on steady conversational subset (top-20 tenants) but net savings only ~4.3% due to CPU overheads and increased cache churn
Notes: numbers assume 90% token-level cost avoided on hits and ignore model tier fallback costs. All dollar figures are illustrative and tied to baseline cost assumption in assumptions section.
recommendations: 1) Prototype Dynamic-target allocation in a single region with opt-in for 10 mature customers (top-20 traffic). Focus on metrics: per-tenant hit-rate, end-to-end P50/P95 latency, adoptability. 2) Implement telemetry to track cross-tenant eviction events and noisy-neighbor indicators before changing default policy. 3) Offer per-tenant soft-reserve product: allow customers to buy a minimum cache allocation for predictable hit-rate; bill as a small monthly commitment and surface ROI in Console. 4) Limit prefetch to tenants with >5% reuse-per-session threshold to avoid negative net. 5) Add simulation harness to CI that can run nightly on incoming usage snapshots to recommend reserve percentages for the next billing cycle.
